hero.title: Public Health in Italy
hero.subtitle: Pursue accredited Public Health programs in Italy, combining epidemiology, public healthcare management, and international health policy. Gain valuable perspectives on Mediterranean health demographics and European public health frameworks.

highlights.degree: Master of Science in Public Health
highlights.eligibility: Recognised academic qualification + English / Italian proficiency

overview: At Italy's universities, international students can study public health, health care management, health economics, epidemiology and health policy. If you are interested in disease prevention, community health, healthcare planning and improving health services, you can take a look at relevant bachelor's, master's and research programs at Italian universities.

Public Health in Italy is a good study choice for students wishing to learn about how healthcare systems work, disease prevention and the effect of public policies on population health. Students may study statistics, health promotion, research methods, healthcare administration and health policy, depending on the program.

Studying Public Health in Italy can provide Indian students the chance to get a feel for European healthcare systems and international academic settings if they opt to study abroad. Edu-Hawk Worldwide assists students with selecting the appropriate courses, understanding university requirements, preparing application documents and navigating the international admission process.

sections.title: Why Study Public Health in Italy?

items: In Italy there are universities, public health care institutions and interdisciplinary study opportunities. Students can combine public health with health care management, economics, statistics and social policy.
Key reasons to consider Public Health in Italy include:
International learning environment: Study alongside students from different countries and backgrounds.
Healthcare system exposure: Understand healthcare delivery, prevention strategies and population health challenges.
Specialisation opportunities: Explore epidemiology, health promotion, health policy, biostatistics and healthcare management, depending on the programme.
Research-oriented learning: Some programmes emphasise data analysis, research methods and evidence-based decision-making.
European academic experience: Experience life and education in Italy while developing an international perspective.
Potential financial support: Eligible students may explore university scholarships, regional benefits and tuition reductions.
Students considering Study Public Health in Italy should compare each course's language, curriculum, practical training opportunities, fees and career outcomes before applying.
Universities may offer public-health-related education through dedicated programmes or closely related degrees. The exact course title and curriculum vary by institution.

These programs may offer different professional roles to the graduates.

sections.title: Top Universities in Italy
sections.lead: Explore top public research universities in Italy offering English-taught degrees, historic campuses, and generous regional scholarships.

unis.name: University of Bologna
unis.desc: The University of Bologna offers master's-level programmes relevant to healthcare systems and policy. Its Health Economics and Management programme for the 2026/27 academic year is taught in English and includes areas such as healthcare management, health economics and policy. The university also offers Economics and Public Policy, with a health economics, management and policy pathway. These options may be suitable for students interested in healthcare administration, policy development, health economics or management of healthcare institutions.

sections.title: Eligibility to Study Public Health in Italy

items: Eligibility depends on the level of study and the chosen programme.
For undergraduate programmes
Students may generally need:
An officially recognized secondary school qualification equivalent to the Italian matricola.
Science subjects where relevant to the course.
Proof of proficiency in the language of instruction of the program.
Any entrance examination or other requirements as the university may require.
For master's programmes
Applicants may generally need:
An approved bachelor's degree in public health, life sciences, medicine, biology, health sciences, statistics, economics or other approved subject, depending on the course.
academic credits or subject prerequisites that are relevant.
Minimum academic grade (if applicable).
Knowledge of English or Italian language.
CV, motivation letter or other selection documents, if relevant.
For doctoral programmes
Applicants will normally have a relevant master's degree, a relevant research background and any research proposal, interview or selection documents required by the doctoral program.

Students planning to Study Public Health in Italy should always check the exact admission requirements. A degree in healthcare management or health economics may have different prerequisites from an epidemiology or public health science programme.

sections.title: Admission Requirements for Public Health in Italy

items: Universities may take into consideration academic background, subject prerequisites, language ability and suitability of previous studies.
Common requirements include:
Recognition of prior learning.
Certificates and academic transcripts.
Proof of English or Italian language proficiency, if required.
Letter of motivation or statement of purpose.
Curriculum vitae for admission to selected Master and research programs.
Letters of recommendation (if required)
Entrance examination or interview, as may be applicable.
Official translations or authentication of education documents (if required).
The university may request additional documents from Indian applicants to confirm the validity and equivalence of previous qualifications.
Edu-Hawk Worldwide can help applicants to understand the course specific requirements, organize their documentation and prepare a university application plan.

sections.title: Admission Process for Public Health in Italy

items: The admission process generally involves the following steps:
Select an appropriate course: Decide on your objective: public health science, epidemiology, health policy, healthcare management, or health economics.
Short list universities: Compare course content, language of teaching, tuition fees, entry requirements and application deadlines.
See if you qualify: Please ensure that your previous degree and subjects meet the entry requirements of the program.
Prepare documents: Collect transcripts, certificates, passport, language test results and other requested documents.
Send the application: You need to apply on the university's official admission portal and also appear for any test or interview if required.
Get your admission decision: Follow the university's instructions for acceptance and enrollment.
Complete International Pre-Registration: The procedure for obtaining an Italian study visa is typically followed via Universitaly by those requiring one.
Apply for Student Visa: Deposit the required documents at the competent Italian diplomatic mission. Admission or pre-enrolment does not guaranty a visa approval.
Preparing for arrival: Before you travel make arrangements for accommodation, insurance and other practicalities.
Universitaly portal publishes procedures for international students. Applicants should check the rules and deadlines that apply to their year of study.
Edu-Hawk Worldwide can help students organise these steps, shortlist suitable programmes and understand the documentation required for applications.
Public health careers do not all follow the same professional pathway. Requirements depend on the job, employer, degree and country where a graduate intends to work.
For example:
Public health research: Roles in research may require a relevant postgraduate degree, research experience or a PhD.
Healthcare management: Employers may be looking for relevant academic qualifications, administrative skills and practical experience.
Epidemiology and biostatistics: Quantitative skills and appropriate training often relevant.
Regulated healthcare professions: Clinical positions may require separate professional qualifications, registration or credential recognition.
Employment in India: Graduates should verify the requirements of the particular employer, institution and any relevant professional or government body.
A public health degree does not automatically qualify a person to practice medicine, nursing or other health care regulated profession.
Before choosing Public Health in Italy , students should identify their intended career and confirm whether the selected qualification is suitable for that role.

sections.title: Career Opportunities After Public Health in Italy

items: Graduates may explore roles in public health, healthcare administration, research, policy analysis and health-related organisations, depending on their qualifications and experience.
Potential career paths include:
Public health programme assistant or coordinator
Epidemiology research assistant
Health policy analyst
Healthcare management executive
Public health research associate
Health data analyst

Monitoring and evaluation officer
Research project coordinator
NGO or community health programme officer
Potential employers include research institutes, universities, hospitals, public agencies, health care companies, non-governmental organizations and international development organizations.

Career prospects depend on the content of the program, language skills, practical experience, work authorization and local recruitment requirements. Some positions may require advanced degrees or technical expertise.

For students pursuing Study Public Health in Italy , developing skills in data analysis, research methods, programme evaluation, communication and health policy can help strengthen their professional profile.

Valid passport.
Secondary school certificates for undergraduate applications.
Bachelor's degree certificate for master's applications.
Master's degree certificate for doctoral applications, where applicable.
Academic transcripts and marksheets.
English or Italian language proficiency results, if required.
CV or résumé.
Statement of purpose or motivation letter.
Letters of recommendation, where required.
Portfolio or research proposal, if applicable.
Official translations of documents, where required.
Document verification or declaration of comparability, if requested by the university.

Proof of financial means, accommodation and insurance, as required for the visa application.
Document requirements vary by university, qualification and consular procedure. Applicants should use the official university and visa checklists for the relevant intake.

faq.question: Can Indian students study public health in Italy?
faq.answer: Yes. Indian students can apply for eligible Italian university programs, if they meet the academic, language and documentation requirements. Admission depends on individual program.

faq.question: Are public health programmes in Italy taught in English?
faq.answer: Several health-related master's programs are in English and others in Italian. Students should check the language of instruction of each program before applying.

faq.question: What are the fees for public health studies in Italy?
faq.answer: Tuition is determined by institution and course. Tuition fees at public universities in Italy generally range from about €900 to €4,000 per year, although individual programs may vary. Private institutions may charge higher fees.

faq.question: Can I get a scholarship to study public health in Italy?
faq.answer: Students who qualify should look into university scholarships, regional financial aid and tuition waivers. Awards are subject to the scheme's academic, financial, nationality and documentation requirements; funding is not guaranteed.

faq.question: What can I do after completing a public health degree in Italy?
faq.answer: Graduates, depending on their qualification and experience, may pursue opportunities in health research, epidemiology, healthcare management, health policy, data analysis, community health and NGO programs. Regulated clinical professions have their own individual licensing and qualification requirements.
